metaDescription: Six 4-inch threshold ramps compared by material, size and load rating, for tall door sills, garage lips and small steps crossed by wheelchairs and walkers.
introParagraphs: Four inches is where a lip becomes a step. A rollator cannot be wheeled over it without tipping, a wheelchair caster stops cold, and even a hand cart bumps hard. A ramp is the practical answer, but a 4 inch rise needs more run than a thin wedge provides.

This lineup covers six ramps built for a 4 inch rise, including heavy rubber, a lightweight foam model, a modular four piece set and a tool-free aluminum kit. We evaluated them from product specs and buyer feedback, comparing size, material, load rating and extras like cord channels.

Each ramp is a fixed height, so measure before you order. Weight capacity and secure placement matter, comfort on a slope varies, and an occupational or physical therapist can advise on device fit for a specific person. Rubber, foam and aluminum each behave differently at this height. Rubber wedges such as the VEVOR stay put through weight alone, the Kritkin foam trades stability for easy carrying, and the DWALE aluminum sections trade a seamless deck for lighter parts. Read the stated size and rating on each product page, since several listings leave out length or width, and confirm the footprint fits the floor space on both sides of your door before ordering anything.

products.name: VEVOR 4 Inch Rubber Threshold Ramp, 35.5 Inch Wide
products.description:
The VEVOR is a 35.5 inch wide natural rubber ramp for a 4 inch rise. The listing describes a slip-proof textured and grooved surface with molded drain channels, and a single channel underneath for cables.

Its printed rating of 33069 lb is a vehicle-class figure that far exceeds any mobility device. In practice the useful traits are the full width coverage, the grooved top and the molded drains, which keep rain from pooling at an exterior door. The length is not given in the text provided, so check the product page for the run before measuring your floor.

It is the best all-round choice because it combines width, drainage and a single cable channel without the cost in complexity of modular sets. Compared with the VEVOR with three channels at 2200 lb it has a larger stated rating, while the Silver Spring at 600 lb is the more modest figure. Seat it flat and square to the doorway.
products.bestFor: A wide exterior doorway that sees rain and the occasional cord.
pros: 35.5 inch width covers a standard doorway fully
Molded drain channels shed water from the surface
One underside channel can shelter a cable
Textured, grooved top is slip-proof by design
cons: Run length is not given in the listing text
33069 lb rating is far more than a doorway needs
Heavy natural rubber is awkward to relocate

products.name: Silver Spring Rubber 3-Channel Threshold Ramp, 4 Inch
products.description:
The Silver Spring is a solid rubber ramp rated for 600 lb with three channels underneath. The listing says it handles rises up to 4 inches for wheelchairs, scooters and power chairs, and the grooved surface is meant to give traction in all weather.

A rating of 600 lb is the lowest printed figure in this group, but it still sits above the combined weight of many users and chairs. The point to check is your own total, including a power chair, which can be heavy by itself. The text does not give length or width, so confirm both before ordering.

It is the one to pick if you want a branded, rated rubber ramp with cable channels and do not need a vehicle-class number. Compared with the VEVOR at 33069 lb the capacity is modest, and compared with the DWALE aluminum at 800 lb it is slightly lower. Check the owner guide for your device's weight.
products.bestFor: A power chair or scooter user who will confirm the 600 lb limit.
pros: Three underside channels shelter cables and hoses
Solid rubber stays stable on uneven surfaces
Grooved top is described for all-weather traction
Suited to wheelchairs, scooters and power chairs
cons: 600 lb is the lowest printed rating here
Length and width are not in the listing text
Rubber is heavy to move between doors

products.name: Kritkin 4 Inch Lightweight EVA Threshold Ramp
products.description:
The Kritkin is made of EVA foam and measures roughly 36 inches long, 24 inches wide and 4 inches high. The listing describes the foam as corrosion resistant and wear resistant and sells a single ramp.

Foam is far lighter than rubber or aluminum, so it carries and stores easily. The tradeoff is that foam can compress or shift under a heavy load, and the text provided does not give a weight rating, which is a gap you should resolve on the product page before relying on it with a power chair. The 24 inch width gives a roomy deck compared with narrower models.

A 36 inch run for a 4 inch rise is a decent length, longer than the 19.68 inch YOLOONLY pieces. Choose it if portability and a wide deck matter more than a stated capacity, and avoid it for heavy scooters. Check that it does not slide on your floor.
products.bestFor: Light-duty use where a wide, easy-to-carry deck matters.

36 inch run is a decent length for 4 inches

Corrosion and wear resistant per the listing

Foam may compress under heavy loads

products.name: DWALE 4 Inch Aluminum Entry Door Ramp, 800 lb
products.description:
The DWALE is an aluminum entry ramp rated for 800 lb. The listing says it assembles without tools, with oval insert connectors that slide each section together, and the anodized finish is meant to resist wear.

The high-strength aluminum is lighter than rubber and the sections can be taken apart for storage. A slip-resistant surface is described, and the ramp suits wheelchairs, scooters, electric vehicles and walkers per the text. The size is not given in the text provided, so confirm length and width before you buy.

It is a good choice when you want something lighter than rubber and with a clear rating. Compared with the Nuvium at 1100 lb it has a lower number, while compared with the Silver Spring at 600 lb it has a higher one. Check that every section is fully seated before crossing.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a tool-free aluminum ramp with an 800 lb rating.
pros: Tool-free assembly with sliding oval connectors
800 lb rating beats the Silver Spring at 600 lb
Anodized aluminum is lighter than solid rubber
Sections can be taken apart for storage
cons: Length and width are not in the listing text
Joints between sections need checking before use
Metal surface is slicker than grooved rubber

products.name: YOLOONLY 4 Inch Rubber Threshold Ramp, 7000 lb
products.description:
The YOLOONLY comes as two rubber curb ramps, each 19.68 inches long, 11.81 inches wide and 4 inches high, rated for 7000 lb. Each piece has two reserved holes and matching connectors, according to the listing, and the straight-grained rubber is described as compression resistant.

Having two ramps lets you set one at each wheel path or line them up for a wider span. A 19.68 inch run for a 4 inch rise is fairly steep, so it is not the gentle choice. The 7000 lb rating is a vehicle-class figure.

It makes sense for a garage lip where each wheel path needs its own ramp. Compared with the Kritkin at 36 inches in length, each piece is much shorter, so the slope is steeper. Compared with the HOXWELL at 3000 lb it states a higher capacity.
products.bestFor: A wheel-path setup at a garage or driveway lip.
pros: Two ramps cover each wheel path separately
7000 lb rating is well above any device weight
Connectors let you link the pieces
Compression-resistant rubber suits daily use
cons: 19.68 inch run is steep for a 4 inch rise
Two narrow decks need careful wheel alignment
No surface gap between ramps unless linked

products.name: HOXWELL Modular Threshold Ramps, 4 Inch, 4 Pieces
products.description:
The HOXWELL is a four piece modular set with 1, 2, 3 and 4 inch rises that can be stacked or separated to suit different thresholds. The listing states a 9 degree slope and a rating of 3000 lb, and describes a non-slip tread pattern in a new, odor-free material.

A 9 degree slope is the one clear incline figure among these six, and it is gentler than the steep short wedges. The modular design lets one kit cover several lips around a house, from a 1 inch sill up to a 4 inch step. The cost is seams where the pieces join, which can catch a small wheel if they are not fully seated.

It suits a household with several different lips to cover. Compared with the YOLOONLY at 7000 lb it has a lower printed rating, while the stated slope gives it an edge on gentleness. Check each join before crossing.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A 4 inch ramp is for a 4 inch lip or a little less, and an error of half an inch leaves a bump. Measure from the lower floor to the top of the sill at the crossing point. The HOXWELL covers 1, 2, 3 and 4 inch lips in one kit, while the VEVOR, Silver Spring and Kritkin are fixed at 4 inches. If your reading is higher, buy a taller ramp.

For a 4 inch rise, a common guideline is 12 inches of run per inch, or 48 inches, and every ramp here is shorter. The Kritkin at 36 inches is a good length, the YOLOONLY at 19.68 inches is steep, and the HOXWELL states a 9 degree slope. A steep ramp is harder to push and can tip a light chair. Choose the longest run your space allows.

A wide deck forgives a wandering wheel. The VEVOR is 35.5 inches wide and the Kritkin 24 inches, while the YOLOONLY gives two 11.81 inch decks. Measure your device's wheelbase and track width. A narrow pair of decks is fine for a steady wheelchair but harder with a scooter.

Ratings range from the Silver Spring at 600 lb to the VEVOR at 33069 lb. A power chair can be heavy on its own, so add the chair, the user and anything carried. The Silver Spring's 600 lb may be tight for a heavier power chair, while the DWALE at 800 lb and HOXWELL at 3000 lb leave more margin. The Kritkin gives no figure.

Rubber stays put and feels solid, as on the VEVOR and YOLOONLY. EVA foam on the Kritkin is light but can shift or compress, and aluminum on the DWALE is light but slicker. Match the material to how often you will move the ramp. A fixed doorway favors rubber.

Modular sets like the HOXWELL and aluminum kits like the DWALE have seams to check. Cable channels such as the Silver Spring's three help if a cord crosses. Drain channels on the VEVOR help at wet entries. Choose the features you will actually use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Rise and slope
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked each listing for a 4 inch rise and compared run and stated angle. The Kritkin's 36 inch run is the longest stated, the HOXWELL states 9 degrees, and the YOLOONLY's 19.68 inch run is the shortest. Missing lengths were flagged.

howWeEvaluated.title: Deck width and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared widths. The VEVOR at 35.5 inches covers a doorway, the Kritkin offers 24 inches, and the YOLOONLY offers two 11.81 inch decks. We favored fit for common devices.

howWeEvaluated.title: Load rating
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared maker-printed capacity. The VEVOR at 33069 lb and YOLOONLY at 7000 lb lead, the HOXWELL sits at 3000 lb, the DWALE at 800 lb and the Silver Spring at 600 lb. These are listing figures, not independent measurements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and weight
howWeEvaluated.description: We contrasted heavy rubber, light EVA foam and anodized aluminum. Rubber is stable, foam is portable and aluminum is a middle path. Buyer feedback on odor and shifting informed the ranking.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras and setup
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted cord channels, drain channels and tool-free assembly. The Silver Spring has three channels, the VEVOR has one plus drains, and the DWALE assembles without tools. No hands-on testing is claimed.

faq.q: Is a 4 inch ramp too steep for a wheelchair?
faq.a: It depends on the run. A common guideline is 12 inches of run per inch of rise, so 48 inches for 4 inches. The Kritkin at 36 inches is close, while the YOLOONLY at 19.68 inches is steeper. Comfort varies by user and chair, so ask a therapist.

faq.q: Do I need the 33069 lb rating?
faq.a: No. That figure reflects vehicle-class use. A person and a chair weigh a small fraction of it. For a doorway, 600 lb or 800 lb may be adequate, but always add up your own total weight.

faq.q: Can the modular set cover several doors?
faq.a: Yes, the HOXWELL kit includes 1, 2, 3 and 4 inch pieces. Seams can catch small wheels, so check each join before crossing. A single wedge avoids joints when you only have one lip.

The Kritkin's EVA foam is lightweight and wear resistant per the listing, but no load rating is given in the text provided. Foam can compress or shift under heavy loads. Confirm a rating on the product page and avoid it for heavy scooters.
Rubber ramps with drain channels, such as the VEVOR, handle rain well. Aluminum like the DWALE can be slick when wet unless the surface is textured. Keep the ramp clear of leaves and ice.

faq.q: How do I keep a ramp from sliding?
faq.a: Place it flat on dry floor and push it with your foot to test. Heavy rubber stays put better than foam. If it creeps, reposition it or choose a heavier model. Listings for the YOLOONLY mention reserved holes and connectors, which may help when pieces are linked, but confirm on the product page how any fixing is meant to work. An occupational or physical therapist can also advise on setup for a specific person.

faq.q: What if my lip is taller than 4 inches?
faq.a: Do not stack a fixed 4 inch wedge on a 5 inch lip and hope for the best, because the leftover edge still stops wheels. Measure again and look at a taller ramp or a longer portable ramp instead. The HOXWELL kit tops out at 4 inches, so it will not solve a taller rise.
